text:
B: Hi. Hello.
A: Hello.
B: Er, I'm Adam. Shipley, near Bradford.
A: Tomas. Milton Keynes.
B: Right.
A: Mm.
B: What do you do, then?
A: Factory. I run injection moulding machines, plastic packaging. Shifts.
B: Oh, right. Are they long, the shifts?
A: Twelve hours. Four on, four off. You?
B: Stonemason. Repair work, old buildings, mostly sandstone.
A: Stone. By hand?
B: A lot of it, yeah. Saws for the rough cut, then it's chisels and mallets for the face. Er, it's quite slow.
A: In my town in Lithuania, old church, they repair it maybe five years. Every summer some men with scaffolding. Nobody knows when it finish.
B: Ha. That sounds about right, to be honest. You find one problem, then there's another behind it. Do you go back much?
A: Once, twice a year. Summer. My mother is there.
B: That's nice.
A: Is okay. Flight from Luton, which is nightmare.
B: I've only flown from Leeds Bradford. That's not much better, it's on top of a hill, always foggy.
A: Mm.
B: Er, what do you do on your days off, then? Four days is quite a lot.
A: I walk. Long walks, around the lakes, canal. Alone, with podcast.
B: Oh, same. I go up on the moors, Ilkley, Baildon. Mostly on my own, or one mate. What podcasts?
A: History mostly. Soviet times, war. I read books also about this.
B: I listen to a lot of history ones. Mostly local stuff, mills, Victorian Bradford. Bit narrow, maybe.
A: Is not narrow. Is where you live.
B: Yeah. That's true, actually.
A: You live alone?
B: Er, no. With my mum and dad. I moved back after a break-up. I'm saving for a deposit, a little terrace round here.
A: Me also, saving. I have spreadsheet, every month. How much is terrace there?
B: Round Shipley, a two-up two-down, maybe a hundred and forty, hundred and fifty now. It was a lot less five years ago.
A: Hundred fifty. In Milton Keynes, for this money you get garage. Maybe.
B: Ha. Yeah, that's what everyone says. It still feels a long way off, though.
A: You live with parents, you pay small rent, you save more. Is smart. Not step back.
B: Er, I suppose so. Didn't feel like it when I moved.
A: Feeling is one thing. Numbers is other thing.
B: Fair point.
